title: SFI and ABVP members clash over rival bookstalls in Kolkata
seoTitle: Kolkata SFI and ABVP bookstall clash

tea.why: The groups clashed over the right to set up bookstalls on College Street and ideological disagreements regarding the books being sold.
tea.want: SFI sought to operate a bookstall; ABVP demanded to set up a rival stall and objected to the content of SFI's history books.
tea.changed: Nov 18: Police separated the groups with barricades, and SFI members left the area by 7 p.m.

summary: On November 18, 2026, members of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) clashed at College Street in Kolkata. The confrontation began when SFI activists attempted to set up a bookstall with police permission. ABVP members arrived, challenged the permission, and objected to the sale of books concerning communist history. The situation escalated into a standoff involving the throwing of stones, eggs, firecrackers, and water bottles. Police intervened by installing steel barricades to separate the two groups and eventually permitted the ABVP to set up a separate stall. During the event, Left Front chairperson Biman Bose was confronted with slogans by ABVP members. Police reported that traffic was suspended during the incident, but no critical injuries or arrests occurred by the evening.
demands: Right to sell books on nationalism
response: Kolkata Police deployed a large contingent, installed steel barricades to separate the groups, and permitted both organizations to operate stalls on opposite sides of the barricade to maintain order.

arrests.text: Police stated no arrests were made until 7 p.m.

injuries.text: Police stated no one sustained any critical injury.

updates.text: SFI activists began setting up a bookstall in the morning after receiving police permission.
ABVP members arrived, challenged the SFI stall, and began vandalizing books, leading to a standoff.
Police installed barricades to separate the groups and allowed ABVP to set up a rival stall.
SFI members departed the area by 7 p.m.
